metaDescription: Senior UI/UX and product design for UK software teams: a shared working day, WCAG 2.2 AA and GDPR-aware flows, GBP invoicing and full IP assignment.
h1: A senior design partner for UK software teams, in your working day
subtitle: India to the UK is a 4.5-hour offset: a genuinely shared working day rather than a handoff. We design for UK teams with GDPR-aware flows, WCAG 2.2 accessibility and the documentation that public-sector-adjacent buyers expect.
author: Designit

cta.heading: Same working day, senior design team
cta.body: Most UK clients start with a two-week UX audit as a low-risk way to test the working relationship.

sections.heading: What UK software teams tend to need

items.title: UK GDPR shapes the interface
items.body: Consent, data minimisation and subject-access rights all surface as design decisions, not just backend concerns.

items.title: A higher accessibility bar
items.body: The Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations set WCAG 2.2 AA, and the expectation increasingly reaches suppliers and enterprise buyers.

items.title: Senior capacity is scarce
items.body: Senior product design salaries and long hiring cycles mean many teams can't get senior help in the quarter it matters.

items.title: Offshore has meant handoffs
items.body: Layers and overnight lag are the usual failure. With a 4.5-hour offset and senior designers working directly with you, neither is structural.

sections.heading: How we work with UK teams

items.title: Time zones
items.body: India is 4.5 hours ahead of GMT, so our afternoon is your morning. Calls at civilised hours for both sides, answers the same day.

items.title: Contracting
items.body: GBP invoicing, UK-standard NDAs and full IP assignment on payment.

items.title: GDPR-aware flows
items.body: Consent and data-collection journeys designed with your DPO or counsel so compliance and conversion aren't opposed.

items.title: WCAG 2.2 AA
items.body: Designed in from the start, with conformance documentation for procurement.

sections.heading: Remote, and upfront about it
paras: We are an India-based studio working with UK clients remotely, with no UK office, and we would rather say so. For UK public-sector procurement we would work as a subcontractor rather than a prime supplier.

faq.q: How does the time difference work with UK teams?
faq.a: India is 4.5 hours ahead of GMT, so our afternoon is your morning and we share a genuine working day. Of the markets we serve remotely, the UK has the most workable overlap.

faq.q: Do you have a UK office?
faq.a: No. We are an India-based studio working with UK clients remotely. We provide GBP invoicing, UK-standard NDAs and IP assignment, a shared working day and senior designers rather than an account layer.

faq.q: Do you design to WCAG 2.2 and UK accessibility requirements?
faq.a: Yes. We design to WCAG 2.2 AA from the start and provide conformance documentation, because retrofitting accessibility is consistently more expensive.

faq.q: How do you handle UK GDPR in design?
faq.a: As a design problem rather than a legal paste-in. Consent requests, sign-up data minimisation and subject-access journeys are interface decisions, worked through with your DPO or counsel.

faq.q: Can you work with UK public sector or regulated clients?
faq.a: We design for regulated, precision-critical environments and to public-sector accessibility standards. For UK public-sector procurement we would be a subcontractor rather than a prime.
